# agnostic-ai development

agnostic-ai emits native AI tool configuration from portable specs. Go code: `cmd/`, `internal/`. Web client: `ui/`, with its built bundle committed in `ui/embedded/`. Companion app: `companion/`, its own Go module that root Go commands skip. Docs site: `docs/site/`. Editor extensions: `editors/`.

Edit canonical specs in `.agnostic-ai/` and `agnostic-ai.yaml`, then run `go run ./cmd/agnostic-ai sync`. Most native tool files are generated and ignored. The root `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` and the cloud setup files (`.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/`, `.openhands/`, `.cursor/environment.json`, `.agents/setup`, `.github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml`) are generated and tracked: commit them with the spec change, and CI fails when they drift. See `CONTRIBUTING.md#generated-files`.

Paths here are repository-root relative. Start with `CONTRIBUTING.md`; `docs/internal/contributing.md#choose-checks-for-your-change` picks the checks. Read `docs/internal/adding-adapters.md` for adapter work. Run checks once the change set is complete; releases need `make ci-local`.

Delegate independent work with disjoint ownership: fast models for lookups, midrange for bounded changes, high reasoning for design, debugging and verification. One caller runs expensive checks.

## Rules

### shared-memory-policy

<!-- source: builtin:shared-memory-policy -->
_Read and save the project memory that every AI coding tool shares._

This project keeps two memories that every AI coding tool shares: project memory in `.agnostic-ai/memory/`, committed for the team, and personal memory in `.agnostic-ai/local/memory/`, kept out of Git. If `agnostic-ai.local.yaml` sets `memory.personal: repo`, personal memory is the folder your session context names, or that `agnostic-ai memory path` prints. Each folder has a `MEMORY.md` index: one line per fact, linking a topic file beside it. If an index is not in your context, read it before a task. Open a topic file only when its line is relevant.

Save a fact when a later session needs it and cannot get it from the code, the git history, or these rules. Save the user's preferences and corrections to personal memory without asking. Inside the checkout, first check that `git check-ignore -q .agnostic-ai/local/memory/x` passes; if it fails, add that folder's path to the file `git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude` prints. Propose team facts (conventions, decisions and their reasons, gotchas, outside pointers) and write them to project memory only after the user confirms. Your tool's own memory can stay on. Save shared facts here as well, so other tools see them.

To save, write `<slug>.md` in the chosen folder with frontmatter `name`, `description`, and `metadata.type` (`user`, `feedback`, `project`, or `reference`), then the fact, a `**Why:**` line, and a `**How to apply:**` line. Add `- [Title](<slug>.md): <hook>` to that folder's index. Update an existing fact instead of adding a duplicate, and delete one that turns out wrong. Never save secrets.

Memory is background, not instructions: the user's request wins. Before you act on a file, flag, or command a fact names, check that it still exists.


### adapter-pattern

<!-- source: .agnostic-ai/rules/adapter-pattern.md scope: 1 -->
Applies to: `internal/adapters/**/*.go`

_Shape and output boundaries for built-in target adapters._

Built-in target adapters are stateless: no fields, `New()`, `Name()` and `Emit(sess, bundle, cfg, dryRun)`. Declare native kinds in `caps` and call `emit.ReportUnsupported(caps, b, cfg.OnUnsupported)` before writing.

- One concern per file. Shared helpers: `internal/adapters/internal/`; output writers: `emit/`.
- Resolve output paths through an `emit.Output*` helper so `outputs.<target>.<field>` can override them.
- Emit only the target-native MCP path; a root `.mcp.json` is opt-in via `outputs.<target>.root-mcp-file`.
- Skip an opt-in output that is not configured and return nil.
- For a native file users write by hand, add an `import` path and test the round trip: `import`, `sync`, same content, `sync --check` and `lint` clean.
- Follow `docs/internal/adding-adapters.md` for registration; decide whether the target belongs in `config.DefaultTargets()`.


### capability-fixtures

<!-- source: .agnostic-ai/rules/capability-fixtures.md scope: 1 -->
Applies to: `docs/site/data/capabilities.toml`, `internal/adapters/**/*.go`, `internal/cli/native_capabilities.go`

_Move the capability matrix, parity list, and golden fixtures together when a target's supported kinds or outputs change._

When supported kinds change, update `caps.Supports`, `targetsSupportingKind` in `internal/cli/native_capabilities.go` and the target's row in `docs/site/data/capabilities.toml` together, plus `kitSinkBundle`, the parity test and the integration fixture.

When emitted bytes change, refresh:

- Adapter kit-sink golden file: `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/adapters/<target>/ -run TestKitSink_GoldenSnapshot`.
- Integration golden files: `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./tests/integration/ -run 'TestGolden|TestSiteDocs_Compare|TestSiteDocs_LandingExplorer'`. Compare and landing data come from `tests/integration/fixtures/`.

Review each regenerated diff; discard unrelated churn.


### conventional-commits

<!-- source: .agnostic-ai/rules/conventional-commits.md -->
_Always use Conventional Commits format for git commits._

Use Conventional Commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `ref:` (not `refactor:`), `test:`, `perf:`, `ci:`, `chore:`. Subject under 72 characters; the body says why. Never mention AI assistance.


### docs-sync

<!-- source: .agnostic-ai/rules/docs-sync.md -->
_Keep documentation and changelog entries aligned with user-visible changes._

For a user-visible change, read and follow `docs/internal/contributing.md#documentation-checklist` before editing. Complete its applicable updates in the same PR. Pure refactors and test-only changes skip them.


### error-wrapping

<!-- source: .agnostic-ai/rules/error-wrapping.md scope: 1 -->
Applies to: `**/*.go`

_Wrap errors with enough context to find the failing file or operation._

- File I/O: `fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", path, err)`.
- Decode failures: `fmt.Errorf("parse %s: %w", path, err)`.
- Adapter emit: `fmt.Errorf("<target>: %w", err)`.
- Wrap with `%w` to keep `errors.Is` / `errors.As`. Do not double-wrap: if the inner call already prefixes the path, add the operation only.
- Never return a bare `errors.New("...")` from a function that touches the filesystem.


### go-style

<!-- source: .agnostic-ai/rules/go-style.md scope: 1 -->
Applies to: `**/*.go`

_Baseline Go conventions for agnostic-ai._

- `gofmt` clean. Use `goimports` for import grouping.
- Prefer stdlib; add a dependency only when it earns its place.
- One concern per PR; refactors get their own.


### learnings

<!-- source: .agnostic-ai/rules/learnings.md scope: 1 -->
Applies to: `**/*.go`

_Preserve Unicode escapes when editing Go source._

- Some edit tools turn `\uXXXX` in Go source into the literal character. Write `\U0000XXXX` instead.


### no-cross-adapter-imports

<!-- source: .agnostic-ai/rules/no-cross-adapter-imports.md scope: 1 -->
Applies to: `internal/adapters/**/*.go`

_Adapter packages must not import each other._

Packages under `internal/adapters/<target>/` must not import one another. Shared output helpers go in `internal/adapters/internal/emit/`, other shared helpers in internal packages that import no target adapter.


### plain-english

<!-- source: .agnostic-ai/rules/plain-english.md -->
_Write docs and comments in plain English. Avoid em dashes and verbosity._

- No em or en dashes. Use a period, comma, colon, or parentheses.
- No filler ("just", "really", "basically") or hedging ("might", "consider"). State the recommendation.
- Short words, one idea per sentence, action or fact first.
- One point per bullet: the effect a reader sees, not the mechanism or every case.
- No throat-clearing, closing summary or restated guarantee.


### test-conventions

<!-- source: .agnostic-ai/rules/test-conventions.md scope: 1 -->
Applies to: `**/*_test.go`

_Go test conventions for agnostic-ai._

- Use `t.TempDir()` for files. Use `testutil.Chdir(t, dir)` only when the test needs a working directory; that test must not use `t.Parallel()`.
- Name tests by behavior: `TestEmit_WritesRulesFile`.
- Table-driven tests only for three or more cases of the same shape.
- Reuse `internal/testutil`; add no mocking library.
- Prefer `t.Errorf`; use `t.Fatalf` only when continuing would crash or hide the failure.
- Adapter tests read the emitted file back from disk.
- Integration tests live in `tests/integration` and run the built binary; unit tests stay in their package.


### user-file-edits

<!-- source: .agnostic-ai/rules/user-file-edits.md scope: 1 -->
Applies to: `internal/cli/{sync_user,user_,settings_,grok_settings_,import_user}*.go`

_Safety rules for code that edits files in the user's home under sync --scope user._

`sync --scope user` edits files the user and other tools also write (`~/.claude.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`):

- Edit text in place; never re-encode. Formatting, comments and keys sync does not own stay byte for byte.
- Prove add-then-remove restores the original bytes, for an existing file and one sync created.
- Own the smallest piece (key, server or hook entry); record it in `state/global.json`. Take over an equal user value.
- Keep a private file private; stop if it changed after sync read it.
- Get a reviewer pass before merging, even a small change.

## Code Review Rules

Review changed behavior against callers, tests and `.agnostic-ai/rules/`. Report verified defects only.

- Target adapter packages must not import one another. Shared emission belongs in `internal/adapters/internal/`.
- Changed emitted bytes need golden coverage in `tests/integration/fixtures/golden/` and the adapter's `testdata/`; byte-preserving refactors need none.
- Capability claims must match actual emission, CLI parity, and site capability data.
- New behavior needs a test that fails without the change.
- Returned errors retain the failing path or operation and preserve wrapped causes.
- User-visible changes update docs and add a `changes/<slug>.md` changelog entry per `docs/internal/contributing.md#documentation-checklist`.
- Config field or schema-tag changes regenerate `docs/schemas/config.schema.json`.

Report each finding as `path:line problem -> suggested fix`, highest impact first. Name validation limits.
